sEn: OpenAI's AI solved ~90 of the top 500 open math problems, showing AI is now superhuman in verifiable domains like math and coding, which will be automated first and accelerate AI R&D before everything else.
sZh: OpenAI 的 AI 解决了 500 个顶级未解数学问题中的约 90 个，表明 AI 在数学和编程等可验证领域已超越人类，这些领域将率先被自动化，进而加速 AI 研发并最终波及一切。
absEn: OpenAI recently released AI-generated solutions to roughly 90 of the top 500 open mathematics problems, a result the author argues should have been historic front-page news but was largely ignored by mainstream media. The core claim is that AI is now superhuman in verifiable domains such as mathematics and coding, while progress in unverifiable domains lags, so math and coding will be automated first, accelerating AI R&D and then everything else. The article examines the mixed reactions from mathematicians, concerns about cryptography and verification, the low error rate and successful Lean formalizations, and the disruption to mathematical careers and training. It concludes that AI is rapidly improving at everything, that verification remains a bottleneck but is holding up well, and that mathematics faces a real problem as its traditional methods of understanding and credentialing are undermined.
absZh: OpenAI 最近发布了针对约 500 个顶级未解数学问题中约 90 个的 AI 生成解答，作者认为这一结果本应成为历史性的头版新闻，却基本被主流媒体忽视。其核心主张是：AI 如今在数学和编程等可验证领域已超越人类，而不可验证领域的进展则相对滞后，因此数学和编程将率先被自动化，从而加速 AI 研发，继而推动其他一切领域。文章考察了数学家的复杂反应、对密码学和验证的担忧、较低的错误率与成功的 Lean 形式化，以及对数学职业和人才培养的冲击。文章最后总结道：AI 在一切方面都在迅速进步，验证仍是瓶颈但表现良好，而数学面临一个真实的问题——其传统的理解与认证方式正被削弱。

contrib.en: OpenAI's AI solved ~90 of top 500 open math problems, a historic but underreported milestone.
contrib.zh: OpenAI 的 AI 解决了约 90 个顶级未解决数学问题中的 90 个，这是一个历史性但被低估的里程碑。

contrib.en: AI is superhuman in verifiable domains like math and coding, but lags in unverifiable domains.
contrib.zh: AI 在数学和编码等可验证领域已超越人类，但在不可验证领域仍落后。

contrib.en: Math and coding will be automated first, accelerating AI R&D and then other fields.
contrib.zh: 数学和编码将首先被自动化，加速 AI 研发，进而推动其他领域。

contrib.en: Low error rate and successful Lean formalizations show verification bottleneck is holding up well.
contrib.zh: 低错误率和成功的 Lean 形式化表明验证瓶颈目前保持良好。

contrib.en: Mathematics faces disruption as traditional understanding and credentialing methods are undermined.
contrib.zh: 数学面临颠覆，传统的理解和认证方法被削弱。

contrib.en: Cryptography under-representation in results raises concerns about potential sudden breakthroughs.
contrib.zh: 结果中密码学的缺失引发了对潜在突然突破的担忧。

limits.en: Verification remains a bottleneck; unverified 58% of results are largely unvetted.
limits.zh: 验证仍是瓶颈；58%的未验证结果大多未经审查。

limits.en: Lean formalization may not confirm theorem matches famous open problem due to term differences.
limits.zh: 由于术语差异，Lean 形式化可能无法确认定理与著名未解决问题的匹配。

limits.en: AI's ability at conjectures and final verification is not yet demonstrated.
limits.zh: AI 在猜想和最终验证方面的能力尚未得到证明。

limits.en: Disrupts mathematical careers and training; traditional PhD and postdoc systems at risk.
limits.zh: 颠覆数学职业和培训；传统的博士和博士后体系面临风险。

limits.en: OpenAI ignored advisory group's request not to test hard problems on private models.
limits.zh: OpenAI 忽视了咨询小组关于不在私有模型上测试难题的请求。

paras.en: 5. You Will Need To Find A New Problem.
paras.zh: 5. 你需要找到一个新问题。

paras.en: 6. Verification or Evaluation Is Not Always Easier Than Generation.
paras.zh: 6. 验证或评估并不总是比生成更容易。

paras.en: 12. Another Mathematical Group Responds.
paras.zh: 12. 另一个数学小组作出回应。

paras.zh: 下面是一系列针对顶级问题的常识性图形解释（当然是由 AI 生成的）。它们看起来是这样的：

paras.en: Maybe, but we haven't yet found a scenario where this is faster in practice.
paras.zh: 也许吧，但我们尚未找到一种在实践中更快的场景。

paras.en: Here are some analyses of the results in algebraic number theory.
paras.zh: 以下是对代数数论中一些结果的分析。

paras.en: What is all of that good for? Ole Lehmann's AI mentions applications for fusion research, portable body scanners, matching systems, tissue scans, quantum sensors, and safety checks on self-driving cars and robots, among other things.
paras.zh: 这一切有什么用呢？Ole Lehmann 的 AI 提到了聚变研究、便携式人体扫描仪、匹配系统、组织扫描、量子传感器，以及自动驾驶汽车和机器人的安全检查等应用。

paras.en: Quasi-RH is not the full Riemann hypothesis, but it is sufficient for many purposes, such as computing square roots modulo a prime quickly without coin flipping, or getting a much better estimate of the number of primes below a given number, and a sibling paper gets to the core of Artin's 1927 primitive root conjecture.
paras.zh: 准黎曼假设（Quasi-RH）并非完整的黎曼假设，但对许多用途而言已经足够，例如无需抛硬币即可快速计算模素数的平方根，或对给定数值以下的素数数量给出更好的估计；而一篇姊妹论文则触及了 Artin 1927 年原根猜想的本质。

paras.en: Fable 5.1's top 100 were 59% today's list, 87% AI, full list at the link.
paras.zh: Fable 5.1 的前 100 名中有 59% 出现在今日榜单中，其中 87% 为 AI，完整列表见链接。

paras.en: When asked about all these math proofs as a hypothetical, the AIs all say that this would be a huge deal, and should be front page news, historic beyond any reasonable comparison, the biggest day in mathematics. Some think it is impossible.
paras.zh: 当被问及所有这些数学证明作为一个假设时，所有 AI 都说这将是一件大事，应该成为头版新闻，其历史意义无可比拟，是数学史上最重要的一天。有些人认为这是不可能的。

paras.en: It turns out this was not front page news. Most people did not hear about it. It should have been, but no one in the news business knows what it means, or thinks people would care.
paras.zh: 事实证明，这并没有成为头版新闻。大多数人没有听说过这件事。它本应成为头版新闻，但新闻界没有人知道这意味着什么，或者认为人们会关心。

paras.en: Joshua Gans starts off his coverage with the actual front page, in order to show us what things The New York Times thought were more important than solving 90 of the top 500 open math problems at once.
paras.zh: Joshua Gans 在他的报道开头展示了实际的头版，以向我们展示《纽约时报》认为哪些事情比一次性解决 500 个顶级未解数学问题中的 90 个更重要。

paras.en: It was a remarkably slow news day otherwise. Much of this is not exactly breaking. Yet no math is to be seen, even in the summaries at the bottom, which even include a generic AI thinkpiece.
paras.zh: 否则，那是一个异常冷清的新闻日。其中大部分内容并不完全是突发新闻。然而，即使在底部的摘要中，也看不到任何数学内容，这些摘要甚至包括一篇泛泛的 AI 思想文章。

paras.en: The counterargument is that there might be a lot of days like this:
paras.zh: 反驳的观点是，可能有很多这样的日子：

full.sec: For Now You Can Still Do Math

paras.en: I like this model of why mathematics is not done quite yet:
paras.zh: 我喜欢这个模型，它解释了为什么数学尚未被完全攻克：

paras.en: We cannot yet show that the AI is better at conjectures or final verification. That will take some additional time, although probably not all that much time.
paras.zh: 我们目前还无法证明 AI 在猜想或最终验证方面更胜一筹。这还需要一些额外的时间，尽管可能不会太久。

paras.en: Verification has to be pretty good or we would have found a lot more errors by now. There are a lot of mathematicians who would love to find a mistake. We know, via the reasoning traces, that a big chunk of effort is going to verification.
paras.zh: 验证必须相当出色，否则我们到现在早就发现更多错误了。有很多数学家会非常乐意找出一个错误。通过推理轨迹我们知道，很大一部分精力都投入到了验证上。

full.sec: You Will Need To Find A New Problem
full.secZh: 你将需要找到一个新问题

paras.en: Scott Aaronson reports on the Mathocalypse.
paras.zh: Scott Aaronson 报告了“数学末日”（Mathocalypse）。

paras.en: Then there is the other kind of ‘new problem,’ where those in denial, who three years ago took comfort in talking about how LLMs could not do math, have to find a new way to explain why anything an AI can do is not real or not meaningful.
paras.zh: 然后是另一种“新问题”：那些否认者，三年前还乐于谈论 LLM 不会做数学，现在必须找到新的方式来解释为什么 AI 能做的任何事情都不是真实的或没有意义的。

paras.en: I do have to tip my hat to the fully general counterargument to all possible AI hype:
paras.zh: 我不得不向对所有可能的 AI 炒作完全通用的反驳脱帽致敬：

paras.en: Whatever AI is good at is Moravec’s paradox. Whatever AI is bad at is why it sucks. Why are you so excited that AI is suddenly superhuman in an increasingly large set of domains, including the exact things we were saying it was dumb for being bad at? Surely this will not extend soon to other domains.
paras.zh: AI 擅长什么都是莫拉维克悖论。AI 不擅长什么就是它糟糕的原因。为什么你们如此兴奋，AI 突然在越来越多的领域变得超人，包括我们之前说它笨的那些它不擅长的领域？当然，这不会很快扩展到其他领域。

full.sec: Verification or Evaluation Is Not Always Easier Than Generation
full.secZh: 验证或评估并不总是比生成更容易

paras.en: The steelman of this critique is to draw a distinction between verifiable versus unverifiable domains.
paras.zh: 这一批评的最强版本是区分可验证领域与不可验证领域。

paras.en: This argument says that whenever you have a verified domain, with known ground truth, AI will quickly become superhuman.
paras.zh: 该论点认为，只要存在一个可验证的领域，且其真实基准已知，AI 就会迅速超越人类。

paras.en: Whereas, if verification is difficult, or all you can do is evaluate in an informal way that requires a human in the loop to avoid biased errors and distorted behaviors, then AI capabilities will lag behind.
paras.zh: 反之，如果验证困难，或者你所能做的只是需要人类介入以避免偏差错误和扭曲行为的非正式评估，那么 AI 能力就会滞后。

paras.en: We were in a weird place for a few years, when pretraining dominated and LLMs were mostly trained on human words. This led to a seemingly non-Yudkowsky world in key ways, with LLMs being relatively excellent at a variety of useful but unverified domains, while being hopeless at math.
paras.zh: 过去几年我们处于一个奇怪的位置：当时预训练占主导，LLM 主要基于人类文本训练。这在关键方面导致了一个看似非 Yudkowsky 式的世界：LLM 在多种有用但未经验证的领域相对出色，却在数学上毫无希望。

paras.en: Now, with post-training dominating, LLMs are again stronger at math and coding, and things again look like you would expect. AI is quickly getting better at everything, but progress in other domains, while super fast compared to almost any other tech ever, is relatively slow for now. Thus, we advance math and coding and similar domains first, which then automate AI R&D, which then accelerates everything else.
paras.zh: 如今，随着后训练占主导，LLM 在数学和编程方面再次变强，情况又回到了你预期的样子。AI 正在迅速提升一切能力，但其他领域的进展——尽管与几乎任何其他技术相比都超快——目前相对缓慢。因此，我们首先推进数学、编程及类似领域，这些领域随后自动化 AI 研发，进而加速其他一切。

paras.en: Justin Drake notices that there is a striking under-representation of cryptographic breakthroughs among the results. As in, zero of the 719 abstracts mention cryptography, LWE or discrete logs.
paras.zh: Justin Drake 注意到，在这些结果中，密码学突破的代表性明显不足。也就是说，719 篇摘要中没有任何一篇提到密码学、LWE 或离散对数。

paras.en: One option is that AI is relatively weak at cryptography, another is luck or that OpenAI didn’t have cryptography in its initial problem set (perhaps to avoid exactly this issue?), or perhaps the government or OpenAI are censoring those results.
paras.zh: 一种可能是 AI 在密码学方面相对较弱，另一种可能是运气，或者 OpenAI 最初的问题集中没有包含密码学（也许正是为了避免这个问题？），又或者政府或 OpenAI 正在审查这些结果。

paras.en: Justin calls for a ‘bunker mode’ for the blockchain industry, to protect against sudden mass breakthroughs.
paras.zh: Justin 呼吁区块链行业进入‘掩体模式’，以防范突然的大规模突破。

paras.en: Vitalik says not to panic, but that there are serious risks to cryptography from potential new math discoveries, including to lattices but not yet to hashes.
paras.zh: Vitalik 表示不必恐慌，但潜在的数学新发现确实给密码学带来了严重风险，包括对格（lattices）的风险，但目前尚未波及哈希（hashes）。

paras.en: I am guessing Vitalik’s point about botched migrations is highly underappreciated. It is very easy, in crypto, to lose fantastical amounts of money from stupid mistakes, the same way you can lose it from hacks or tech failures.
paras.zh: 我猜测 Vitalik 关于迁移失败的观点被严重低估了。在加密货币领域，愚蠢的错误很容易让你损失天文数字的金钱，就像黑客攻击或技术故障一样。

paras.en: Yes, you should worry, especially given that OpenAI's breakthroughs here did not involve trying maximally hard.
paras.zh: 是的，你应该担心，尤其是考虑到 OpenAI 在此处的突破并未涉及竭尽全力。

paras.en: Gary Marcus is defending his position by saying that the neural networks involved had a separate symbolic system, so none of this counts and he was right all along, and if 'that's over your head' you probably shouldn't be commenting on AI. The polite response is that the distinction does not matter in practice.
paras.zh: Gary Marcus 在为他的立场辩护时称，所涉及的神经网络有一个独立的符号系统，因此这一切都不算数，而他一直都是对的；如果“这超出了你的理解范围”，你大概就不该对 AI 发表评论。礼貌的回应是：这种区分在实践中并不重要。

paras.en: Here are 100+ reactions from various different people in mathematics. A lot of them are very not happy about how OpenAI handled this, especially that so many of the papers were 'unreadable slop' rather than having been made nice first, or that OpenAI solved these problems at all. If you want to know 'what are the mathematicians thinking' this is a great resource.
paras.zh: 这里有来自数学界不同人士的 100 多条反应。其中很多人对 OpenAI 处理此事的方式非常不满，尤其是那么多论文是“无法阅读的垃圾”，而不是先被整理得像样一些，或者对 OpenAI 竟然解决了这些问题感到不满。如果你想知道“数学家们在想什么”，这是一个很好的资源。

paras.en: Here is Terence Tao's serious response, which focuses on how this disrupts the work:
paras.zh: 这里是陶哲轩的严肃回应，重点在于这如何扰乱了工作：

paras.en: Here is another report from mathematician-land. People do not seem thrilled.
paras.zh: 这里是来自数学界的另一份报告。人们似乎并不兴奋。

paras.en: Mathematicians seem to think of math as their playground, and rather than be happy about the problems being solved they feel their toys are being taken away. There is a struggle between wanting to know, and wanting to try to solve, and wanting the credit, and wanting solutions to be found at all. What do you actually care about most?
paras.zh: 数学家们似乎把数学视为自己的游乐场，他们并不为问题被解决而高兴，反而觉得自己的玩具被拿走了。在想知道、想尝试解决、想获得荣誉，以及想问题最终被解决之间，存在着一种挣扎。你真正最关心的是什么？

paras.en: To be smart enough to be a mathematician, and also choose to be a mathematician instead of the many other better-paying things you could do, at least kind of requires some of the attitude that leads to cartoons where someone tells the mathematician someone found an application for their work, and the mathematician panics. Definitely #NotAllMathematicians, of course.
paras.zh: 要聪明到足以成为数学家，并且还选择成为数学家，而不是去做许多其他薪水更高的事情，至少需要某种态度，这种态度导致了那些漫画：有人告诉数学家，有人为他们的工作找到了应用，然后数学家就慌了。当然，绝对不是所有数学家都这样。

paras.en: I am highly sympathetic. I really am. There could I have gone. That attitude has great value, not only inherently, but also exactly because following such curiosity leads to some of the most valuable discoveries that you would otherwise miss.
paras.zh: 我深表同情。真的。我本可能走上那条路。这种态度具有巨大价值，不仅本身如此，而且恰恰因为追随这样的好奇心会带来一些你原本会错过的、最有价值的发现。

paras.en: It is also totally reasonable to focus on how things impact you and yours. That’s what hits home, and it is the part you can most control and are forced to face.
paras.zh: 专注于事情如何影响你和你的亲人，也完全合理。那才是切中要害的，也是你最能控制、并被迫面对的部分。

paras.en: If your response is ‘well everyone’s passions are going away and the AIs come for us all’ then that’s worse. You know why that’s worse, right? Nor does it make this easier. There are some people out there reacting to these understandable reactions in truly vile ways. I urge them to stop.
paras.zh: 如果你的回应是‘好吧，每个人的热情都在消失，AI 要来对付我们所有人了’，那就更糟了。你知道为什么更糟，对吧？这也不会让事情变得更容易。有些人正以真正恶劣的方式回应这些可以理解的反应。我敦促他们停止。

paras.en: Mathematics is facing a real problem here. If the AIs prove all the theorems, then our current methods of getting good at understanding math stop working. The traditional way you understand problems is by working to solve them and a solution is often not worth so much if no one understands it:
paras.zh: 数学在这里面临一个真正的问题。如果 AI 证明了所有定理，那么我们目前用来精通数学理解的方法就失效了。理解问题的传统方式是努力解决它们，而如果没有人理解，一个解决方案往往就不那么有价值：

paras.en: There are other ways to train understanding, but it could take a while to develop them, and they will require more motivation, especially intrinsic motivation.
paras.zh: 还有其他训练理解力的方法，但开发它们可能需要一段时间，而且它们需要更多动力，尤其是内在动力。

paras.en: This also destroys the system of PhDs and postdocs, since the problem you are looking to solve or the grant you want can get pulled out from under you at any time.
paras.zh: 这也摧毁了博士和博士后的体系，因为你想要解决的问题或你想申请的经费随时可能被抽走。

paras.en: Some solutions were elegant and pretty cool. For example, the 9/4 matrix multiplication paper is 13 pages and bounds Strassen's spectral characters directly. We've seen a bunch of people, after seeing their favorite problem get solved, share their 'aha' moment reading the proof.
paras.zh: 有些解法优雅且相当酷。例如，那篇关于 9/4 矩阵乘法的论文只有 13 页，直接给出了 Strassen 谱特征的界。我们看到许多人在自己钟爱的问题被解决后，分享了他们阅读证明时的“顿悟”时刻。

paras.en: I am with Wendigo that it is kind of weird and terrible that we are seeing all these new tiny improvements to previously elegant bounds on calculations, that have almost zero practical benefit.
paras.zh: 我同意 Wendigo 的看法：我们看到所有这些对先前优雅的计算界做出的微小改进，却几乎没有任何实际益处，这有点奇怪且糟糕。

paras.en: Now how about if we push it down to \((1/2)^{59}\)? Then to \((1/2)^{34}\)? And then to \((1/2)^{14}\)?
Anyone can keep doing things like this. All you need is a Codex subscription.
paras.zh: 任何人都可以一直这样做。你只需要一个 Codex 订阅。

paras.en: Here is the full statement by the leading advisory group:
paras.zh: 以下是该主要顾问小组的完整声明：

full.secZh: 另一个数学团体的回应

paras.en: Some look at what is happening, and cry out 'NO!'
paras.zh: 有些人看到正在发生的事情，会大声喊出‘不！’

paras.en: They are going to need a much better plan than this statement.
paras.zh: 他们需要的，远比这份声明要高明得多。

paras.en: Do not be fooled into thinking this group, the 'Association for Human Mathematics,' is a big deal. There are hundreds of thousands of mathematics PhDs, and this group has 809 members. I include it because it perfectly embodies an attitude, nothing more.
paras.zh: 不要被误导，以为这个名为‘人类数学协会’的团体有什么了不起。数学博士有成千上万，而这个团体只有 809 名成员。我把它列出来，只是因为它完美体现了一种态度，仅此而已。

paras.en: Whatever you think of the rest of the statement, they are not wrong that the entire exercise here was directly against what the mathematics advisory group (AGMAI) wanted. AGMAI's central ask was that OpenAI was asked to not test hard problems on private internal models. That request, regardless of what you think of it, got fully ignored.
paras.zh: 无论你对这份声明其余部分怎么看，有一点他们没说错：这里的整个做法，直接违背了数学咨询小组（AGMAI）的意愿。AGMAI 的核心诉求是，OpenAI 被要求不要在私有的内部模型上测试难题。这一要求，无论你怎么看，都被完全无视了。

paras.en: OpenAI admits that ‘dump it all on GitHub’ is not exactly meeting the advisory committee’s guidelines. They are exploring better options, and are hoping in the future to also have better-written papers.
paras.zh: OpenAI 承认，“把所有内容一股脑丢到 GitHub 上”并不完全符合咨询委员会的指导方针。他们正在探索更好的方案，并希望未来也能有写得更好的论文。

paras.en: On top of the big drop there was also this, that came out one day earlier, where Anthropic gave their solution to mathematicians to write up before releasing it, attempting to follow the advisory group’s recommendations:
paras.zh: 除了那批大规模发布之外，还有这个早一天出现的内容：Anthropic 在发布之前先把他们的解法交给数学家撰写成文，试图遵循该咨询小组的建议：

paras.en: There was also another stray new math result via GPT that came out right before the massive drop of other math.
paras.zh: 还有另一个零散的、由 GPT 得出的新数学结果，恰好在其他数学成果大规模发布之前出现。

paras.en: The three withdrawals are all consequences of a single sign error.
paras.zh: 这三次撤稿都是同一个符号错误的后果。

paras.en: I love the idea of a website called Retraction Watch. This is one area where OpenAI executed well. Mistakes happen, and even if more are found — and there will almost certainly be more errors found, as the unverified 58% is still largely unvetted — the error rate is impressively low. The important thing is to own the mistakes once they are found. Retractions are often a sign that you are doing something right, not something wrong.
paras.zh: 我很喜欢 Retraction Watch 这个网站的理念。这是 OpenAI 做得很好的一方面。错误在所难免，即便发现更多错误——而且几乎肯定还会发现更多错误，因为那未经核实的 58% 在很大程度上仍未被审查——错误率也低得令人印象深刻。重要的是，一旦发现错误就要勇于承认。撤稿往往表明你做对了某件事，而不是做错了。

paras.en: I liked this explanation from Jon Stokes: Mathematics is great for advanced AIs, especially GPTs, because there is no 'reward hacking.' The answer is the answer; if you do something crazy and out of distribution but it works, then it works.
paras.zh: 我喜欢 Jon Stokes 的这个解释：数学对高级 AI（尤其是 GPT）非常有利，因为不存在“奖励黑客”。答案就是答案；如果你做了疯狂且分布外的事情，但它有效，那它就是有效的。

paras.en: Except, are you sure? One angle is that you can either find a proof or you can find a bug in Lean, and are you sure the math will always be the easier option when you face the world's toughest open problems?
paras.zh: 不过，你确定吗？一个角度是，你要么找到一个证明，要么找到 Lean 中的一个 bug，而当你面对世界上最难的开放问题时，你确定数学总是更容易的选择吗？

paras.en: The bigger risk is that Lean does not confirm that the stated theorem matches up to the famous open problem. Your terms might be different, in ways that are non-obvious at first glance.
paras.zh: 更大的风险是，Lean 并不确认所陈述的定理与著名开放问题相匹配。你的术语可能不同，而且差异乍看之下并不明显。

paras.en: So far, Lean is holding up, as are all the papers with Lean proofs modulo one corrected side claim, which is rather impressive. The system works. There are 3 proofs that have broken so far, and all of them are in the unformalized 58%.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，Lean 经受住了考验，所有带有 Lean 证明的论文也是如此，除了一个被修正的附带声明，这相当令人印象深刻。系统是有效的。目前有 3 个证明被破坏，它们都在未形式化的 58% 中。

paras.en: Of the nine results discussed up top, five are checked in Lean (quasi-RH, matrix multiplication, \(\pi\), Unique Games and Hadwiger), as in the Lean-checked 42%.
paras.zh: 在上面讨论的九个结果中，有五个在 Lean 中检查过（准 RH、矩阵乘法、\(\pi\)、Unique Games 和 Hadwiger），即在 Lean 检查的 42% 中。

paras.en: At some point, you will give the model a task that is substantially harder than some other way to solve 'the problem' of you assigning the task, whether or not the alternative path involves taking over the world. Then you will be the one that has a problem.
paras.zh: 在某个时刻，你会给模型分配一个任务，而解决“你分配这个任务”这一问题，存在某种远比执行该任务更简单的方式——无论这条替代路径是否涉及接管世界。到那时，有麻烦的就会是你自己。
